news.title: Briefing · AI
news.intro1: From the collected posts the AI writes one briefing — not a summary per post, but the overall picture.
news.intro2: Two stages with two providers: Gemini watches the YouTube videos first (the only provider that opens a video URL itself, with its own key). What comes out of that goes, together with the text items, to
news.intro2b: which writes the briefing. If Gemini fails the briefing is still produced — just without video content.
news.intro3: The video is the expensive part, not the text: it is billed by video length. Subtitles would be cheaper, but YouTube no longer serves them to signed-out clients (checked 16 Aug 2026, yt-dlp included).
news.autoHint: Daily, weekly or not at all ("manual only"). Off: by button only. Posts are collected daily regardless.
news.topicsHint: One chapter per topic. The crypto part also gets the Marktradar readings (Fear & Greed, dominance, funding, long/short).
news.researchHint: With a Perplexity key the briefing additionally researches each topic on the web (sources included); with an xAI key, X sources are fetched via Grok — once a day. Both keys live under Access. Without a key the respective step is skipped silently.
news.grokModel: Grok model for the X search:
news.videosHint: Video is the most expensive input type — billed by length. 0 = watch no videos; the briefing then uses only titles and video descriptions.
news.reportModelHint: Empty = your globally configured provider. The briefing is pure text work — a cheaper model often does just as well.
news.resolutionHint: Low costs about 100 tokens per second of video, standard about 300 — three times as much. For spoken market commentary low is enough, because the audio carries the content.
news.costSplit: per run — of which {text} for the text, {n} × {proVideo} for the videos (at 20 minutes each)
news.layoutHint: Combined puts the most important items on top as cards (“top items”, at most three) and sets the rest as articles inside their chapter. Newspaper drops cards entirely, Tiles shows everything as equally sized cards, as before. Which items go on top is decided by the AI as it writes — if it marks none as important, the card row stays empty.
news.scopeHint: Items are the individual points of a chapter — in the newspaper layout, one article each with headline, paragraph and sources. The token cap bounds how long the AI answer may get; it caps the cost rather than setting it.
news.videoTokensHint: own output cap, empty = per level
news.topicChartanalyse: Technical chart analysis top 5 (from sources, with images)
news.customHint: Tone, focus and exclusions for the briefing — applies from the next run. Empty = unchanged.
news.customPlaceholder: e.g.: Write more tersely, no filler. Give the time of each item. Regulation only matters to me when it affects futures. More detail on Ether than on altcoins.
news.customLimits: {n} of {max} characters. The ground rules stay in force: no trade recommendations, no price targets, no forecasts, nothing invented. Every character costs tokens on every run.
news.manualHint: The briefing is only written when you press the button.
news.updatesHint: On top of the daily briefing: at the configured hour the AI searches your sources and the web for what has come in since — news, numbers and dates relevant to crypto and trading. It does not rewrite the briefing, it reports only what is new, and shorter than the briefing.
news.updatesCost: Each interim note costs one research call and one writing call.
news.sendIntro: Who receives the finished briefing. This event is not in the notification table because it is the only one that can go to several readers.
news.browserHint: Short pop-up once a briefing is ready — only while the journal is open.
news.browserGlobalOff: Browser notices are switched off entirely under Notifications.
news.mailOnHint: Only automatic runs send mail. A briefing you triggered yourself stays silent — you are sitting in front of it.
news.mailNoSmtp: SMTP is switched off — enable it under Notifications, otherwise nothing goes out.
news.recipientsHint: Separate with comma, semicolon or line break, at most {max}. All go in the "To" field and see each other.
news.recipientsNone: No valid address — nothing will be sent.
news.recipientsFallback: Empty — the general recipient from Notifications applies ({adresse}).
news.mailHint: The short form says THAT a briefing exists and points to the journal. The full one puts the briefing in the mail itself — handy on the road, but long.
news.mailShort: Short — overall picture and run figures
news.mailMedium: Medium — plus market snapshot and chapter summaries, no individual items
news.mailFull: Full briefing — chapters, items, figures, sources
news.keepHint: How long generated briefings are kept. "By hand" never deletes — every briefing cost money. Cleanup runs once a day; raw posts have their own 30 days.
news.checkHint: One model call (a few cents): what takes effect, what bounces off the hard rules — plus a sharper wording.
news.chartHint: Chart analysis: how old the cited analyses may be, and which horizon they should describe.
news.profilesDescription: Named presets of all fields on this page plus the focus/exclude filters and source selection. On the news page there's only a dropdown to apply them — they're created and edited here.
news.updateProfileTitle: Snapshot the current settings into this profile again
news.sourcesDescription: YouTube channels, RSS feeds, Telegram channels, and X accounts for the news page. Anything you mark as exclude gets hidden by "Temporarily exclude" — and isn't fetched at all. Only title, link, and timestamp are stored, never full text.
news.xSourceHint: About X: runs via the paid Grok search (xAI) — just the handle is enough as the address, e.g. {'@'}saylor. All X sources together cost ONE search per fetch run (roughly $0.005 plus tokens), throttled to at most one search every four hours. Requires an xAI key under "AI settings". Free workarounds (Nitter mirrors) are dead — checked 2026-08-16.
news.tempExcludeOn: On — sources marked as excluded stay out
news.tempExcludeOff: Off — all active sources are fetched
news.quietFilterHint: Filters Truth Social automatically. Posts containing one of the keywords (one per line) disappear from the list and the briefing.
news.focusFilterHint: The opposite of the quiet filter: only posts containing one of the keywords (one per line) remain in the list and the briefing. Empty = no focus, everything stays.
news.colExcludeTitle: Temporarily exclude: the source is neither fetched nor shown while the switch above is on.
news.colVideosTitle: YouTube only: should this source's videos go to Gemini? Each one costs $0.03–0.10.

benachrichtigungen.kanalHinweis: A dash in the email column means the server cannot detect this event on its own. Email checkboxes become available once sending is switched on below.
benachrichtigungen.anderswo: {was} is configured under AI → News — with its own recipient list.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_picycleKreuzung: The 111-day line crosses twice the 350-day line. Historically close to cycle tops — but three times in fifteen years, so a hint, not a statistic.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_picycleVorwarnung: Reporting the cross itself comes too late — it is the signal. A threshold gives you lead time.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_fundingDivergenz: Funding rates for the watched markets diverge between Binance and Bybit. Where one exchange breaks away, the crowded side sits there alone.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_lageberichtFertig: The automatic news briefing was created. Manually triggered ones stay silent.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_kiBerichtFertig: A report or agent run has finished.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_kiGuthabenLeer: A provider stopped accepting requests. While this lasts, briefings and agent runs fail.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_boerseKeinZugang: An exchange rejects the stored API key. While this lasts, no positions arrive from there.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_neueVersion: A newer release is published on GitHub.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_aufzeichnungStumm: A depth stream has delivered nothing across several reconnects — recording data is missing without anyone noticing.
benachrichtigungen.hinweis_importFertig: A CSV or API import has completed.

info.customTimeframe:
Your own time frame for classifying trades, e.g. "Swing 3d".
The built-in Scalp/Daytrade categories follow the minute and hour limits above; a custom frame is assigned by hand.
info.fluxModel:
Which FLUX model paints the share card background.
Larger models cost more per image and take longer; for a card that ends up as a thumbnail that rarely pays off.
info.geminiImageModel:
Which Gemini image model paints the share card — the alternative to FLUX.
Both need their own key and are billed by that provider, not through the AI settings.
info.liveRamp:
The colour scale of the order book heat map.
Viridis and Magma are perceptually uniform — equal colour steps mean equal differences in size. A rainbow scale is not, and there the eye invents edges where there are none.
info.dbPort: The default is 5432. If PostgreSQL runs in a container with a remapped port (often 5433 on a NAS), that is the port that belongs here, not the internal one.
info.boersenLinks: Controls only WHICH links are shown — not whether a coin is actually listed there. Bitunix/Bitget/Pionex still only appear when the coin is actually listed there; the chart (formerly TradingView) always appears if checked.
info.speicher: Display only: database space per module, including indexes. Expand a row to see the individual tables. Recordings and screenshots grow fastest — automatic cleanup (retention) runs independently; this view shows whether it works.
info.laermfilter:
Switches off the sources marked as noise: they are neither fetched nor displayed.
Acts at fetch time — items already stored stay put. Not to be confused with the quiet filter below, which filters by words.
info.wortfilter:
Filters by keyword rather than by source: items containing one of the words disappear from the list and the briefing.
Acts at display time, not at fetch time — so changing the word list retroactively changes what you see.
info.fokusfilter:
The mirror image of the quiet filter: instead of excluding, it only lets through items that contain one of the keywords — e.g. 'Bitcoin' and 'BTC' for a pure BTC focus.
Left empty means 'no focus', not 'nothing gets through'. One of the fields a News Profile (under AI · News) captures.
info.newsProfile:
A profile captures, at creation, exactly the values currently set on this page — rhythm, topics, length, model choice, mail recipient, exclude/focus filters, and which sources are active.
'Apply' writes all of that back; the mail recipient and model choice visibly change along with it if the profile differs — no silent switch.
info.mailSicherheit:
TLS encrypts from the first second (port 465); STARTTLS begins unencrypted and switches over (port 587).
Which one works is decided by the provider. Gmail and Outlook also need an app password — the normal account password is rejected for SMTP.
info.newsRhythmus:
When the briefing is written by itself: daily, weekly or not at all.
"Manual only" does not mean never — the interim notes below run independently, and the button on the news page always works.
info.mailSchrift:
Applies to the text of notification e-mails. A mailbox has no browser-style zoom — the size is fixed when the mail is sent and cannot be changed while reading.
Changes take effect with the next mail; use "Send test mail" to see the result right away.

hype.quadrantHinweis: Top right, trading is following along. Top left, there is talk the market does not follow — that is where bought noise sits. Labelled are the checked finds: green from a safety score of 70, amber from 40, red below; red with a name are the rejected ones. The grey ones stayed under the threshold and were never checked — hover to see their name.
hype.regelnBoerse: For Coin Radar favourites (Bitunix symbols): there is no liquidity pool and no contract check there — turnover, spread and funding are watched instead.

hype.sicherheitHinweis: Anything breaching these never reaches the report — regardless of its hype score.
hype.trittbrettHilfe: Finds whose name contains an established coin or a foreign brand — they bring no idea of their own, only the hope of being mistaken for it. Their score is already reduced.
hype.wachhundHinweis: Watches the favourites on a schedule and fires when something material changes. Critical repeats after 1 hour at the earliest, the rest after 4.
hype.webhookPayload: The webhook posts JSON with regel, schwere, symbol, meldung and daten — a Home Assistant automation filters on trigger.json.schwere == 'kritisch' and starts the lights.
hype.boersenFilterChip: {b} — show only finds tradable there. Selecting several means "on at least one". Unresolved listings stay in.
hype.wachhundAusHinweis: The watchdog is off. Favourites stay saved and visible — they are simply no longer watched, and no new alerts are raised.
hype.gueteTitel: What became of the finds? — outcome tracking
hype.gueteHinweis: After 1, 7 and 30 days we check: does the pair still exist, how did price and liquidity develop? The best passed finds are compared with a sample of those rejected by the safety check (does the filter work?) and a sample of the field below the threshold (does the score work?). A verdict only stands when Fisher's exact test confirms the difference (p < 0.05).
hype.gueteLeer: No measurements yet. They are created after every scan and redeemed after 1, 7 and 30 days.
hype.gueteFehler: Outcome tracking could not be loaded.
hype.spalteSubstanzTitel: Substance score of the project check (website, domain, GitHub) — stands next to hype and safety and is merged with neither
hype.projektHinweis: For the passed finds the radar looks at what is behind the token: the website (content, contract address, placeholder text), the domain age and GitHub (maintained? earlier projects?). No keys; each check is valid for 24 hours.
hype.fruehHinweis: A separate lane ahead of the main check: tokens younger than twelve hours or with less than USD 50,000 liquidity. It measures acceleration — trading, distinct buyers and mentions against the token's own history — not size. Tokens that mature move into the main check on the next scan.
hype.fruehAlarmHinweis: Alerts fire when the score crosses the threshold, at most every 12 hours per token, through the watchdog's channels — and only for what could also be a candidate: contract and project checked, at least three sub-scores, two of them from the market, at least 20 transactions in the last hour. 0 = watch only.
hype.fruehQuelle_geckoterminalNeu: CoinGecko on-chain — new pools with buyer count (own key)
hype.fruehXHinweis: One Grok search per interval (xAI key under Settings → AI). Only cited posts and distinct authors are counted. The price of the last query is shown above the list.
hype.smartHinweis: Wallets from the GMGN, Kolscan or Cielo leaderboards. Only buys the wallet signed and paid itself count. Two wallets on the same token trigger an alert at once. Reading only goes through your own RPC address (e.g. Helius, free tier) — the public Solana node is, per Solana, not meant for applications and is not used.
hype.boersenwachtHinweis: Compares the public market lists of large and mid-sized exchanges, detects new listings and checks whether the radar flagged the token beforehand. No keys.
hype.boersenAlleMelden: Also alert on listings the radar did not know (large exchanges only)
hype.fruehKandidatHinweis: A candidate is an alert-eligible token (contract and project checked, at least three sub-scores, two of them from the market, at least 20 transactions in the last hour) with a score from this value. Deliberately below the alert threshold: the list shows what you should look at, the alert what you must not miss.
hype.einstGemeinsam: Applies to all views — the settings of overview, early phase and exchanges are found in each of them
hype.noteUnbekannt: Unknown — no source measured this. Does not count as 0; the total averages over the other sub-scores.
hype.boerse_binance-spot: Binance spot (only with Binance as market data source)
hype.cgSchluesselFehlt: No key stored — CoinGecko trending, new pools and buyer counts are off.
hype.boersenWahlHinweis: Coinbase, Kraken, KuCoin and Gate are off by default: their terms do not visibly allow using their market data in a sold program — enable at your own responsibility. Upbit, OKX, MEXC and Binance Alpha were removed for licensing reasons.
hype.rugcheckAn: Use RugCheck (Solana: insider networks, liquidity lock, fallback when GoPlus fails)
hype.rugcheckHinweis: RugCheck's terms of use are unclear (keys and paid tiers possible) — hence off by default. Without RugCheck GoPlus checks alone: insider networks stay unknown, and on Solana the liquidity lock is unknown — with "liquidity must be locked" Solana finds then fail.
hype.quellenEntferntHinweis: pump.fun, CoinPaprika and Reddit are no longer connected: their terms do not allow use in a sold program. CoinGecko and its on-chain pools (formerly GeckoTerminal) only run with your own CoinGecko key.
hype.boerse_binance-futures: Binance futures (only with Binance as market data source)
hype.cgSchluesselDa: Key stored — CoinGecko trending and on-chain pools are running.

hype.keinerGeprueft: No find reached the hype threshold in the last run, so none was safety-checked.

hype.projektHinweisFrei: For passed finds the radar looks at what stands behind the token: the website (content, contract address, placeholder text), the domain age, GitHub (maintained? earlier projects?) and, on pump.fun, the creator's history. No key needed; each check is valid for 24 hours.

How fearful or greedy the market is overall right now — it measures mood, not the price.
Extremes are more interesting than the middle, but "extreme fear" is not a buy signal: the state can stay extreme for weeks before it turns.

Where the Bitcoin price sits long-term relative to its historical range, from "sell-off" to "bubble".
The bands shift with every new price — what reads as "cheap" today can be the middle in a year. A mood gauge across years, too coarse for a single trading decision.

Forced liquidations over the last 24 hours. Red = a LONG was closed out (price fell), green = a SHORT.

The view from outside the crypto market: US equity futures, the dollar index, stablecoin flow.

Colour shows tailwind or headwind FOR CRYPTO, not the direction of the market itself: a rising dollar is therefore red. Stablecoin flow is the change in USDT and USDC supply — deliberately not "USDT dominance", which rises arithmetically whenever crypto falls and merely restates the price drop. Inflow or outflow, by contrast, shows real money entering or leaving the market. The Russell 2000 sits next to the Nasdaq as a cross-check: if both move together it is a liquidity or rates move that reaches crypto too; if only the Nasdaq moves it is rotation into a few large caps and rarely carries over.

A historical signal that has coincided with a Bitcoin cycle top in the past.
Three hits on three occasions is an observation, not a rule — an early warning for "careful with leverage", not an exit signal for a single position.
